findings.issue_text: [BUG] The diff commits a git submodule gitlink at ./sentry-repo (mode 160000, commit a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a) with no corresponding .gitmodules entry, so the submodule has no URL and `git submodule update --init` fails with 'no submodule mapping found in .gitmodules for path sentry-repo'. Every CI job or developer environment that initializes submodules errors out on this commit, and the tree carries an unresolvable, unreferenced nested-repo pointer (nothing else in the diff reads sentry-repo/) that must be dropped before merge.

[BUG] `options.get("issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist", [])` raises on every call: sentry's `options.get(key)` accepts only the key (TypeError on the second positional argument) and raises `UnknownOption` for unregistered options, and this diff does not register `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` in sentry/options/defaults.py. `_get_event_stats` calls `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` unconditionally (organization_events_stats.py:220-222), so every request to the organization-events-stats endpoint raises and returns a 500; all new tests pass only because they patch the entire `options` module with a Mock whose `.get` accepts any signature, masking the crash in CI.

[BUG] `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` returns True unconditionally for the errors dataset, but `upsampled_count` is registered only in DiscoverDataset.function_converter (discover.py:1041-1052) and not in the errors dataset's own function_converter, so transformed errors-dataset queries reference a function the errors dataset cannot resolve. An events-stats request with dataset=errors against an all-allowlisted org fails with InvalidSearchQuery for the unknown function 'upsampled_count' (400), breaking the path the helper's own comment declares the primary case ('Always apply for the errors dataset'); no test in the diff covers dataset=errors.

[BUG] The `sum(sample_weight)` aggregation and the tests' expected count of 10 assume a `sample_weight` column populated as 1/client_sample_rate in the queried snuba entity, but the diff establishes neither the column nor any code path mapping the factory's top-level `sample_rate` event field (factories.py) to that column. The new snuba tests fail (sum over unpopulated weights returns 0 instead of 10, or snuba rejects the unknown column), and if the column is absent from the errors entity every upsampled query errors for allowlisted orgs in production.

[BUG] `SnubaParams(start=None, end=None, projects=self.projects)` omits the required `environments` and `organization_id` fields, which have no defaults on SnubaParams, so the constructor raises TypeError. setUp raises for every test in ErrorUpsamplingTest and the entire new unit-test module errors out in CI; the constructed snuba_params is also never used by any test in the file.

[BUG] `self.request.GET = QueryDict("")` assigns to DRF Request's read-only `GET` property (defined without a setter in rest_framework.request.Request), raising AttributeError. setUp crashes before any test runs, and the same assignment recurs in test_is_error_focused_query, so the new unit-test module cannot pass as written; query params must be supplied via RequestFactory's URL data instead of attribute assignment.

[BUG] `_is_error_focused_query` does a raw substring check for 'event.type:error', so a negated query like `!event.type:error` contains the token and is treated as error-focused. For an all-allowlisted org, a discover query `!event.type:error` (transactions-focused) gets `count()` rewritten to `sum(sample_weight)` against the transactions entity where the column does not exist, returning a query error instead of results.

[ADVISORY] `invalidate_upsampling_cache` has no caller anywhere in the diff and no hook exists (options-change handler, admin UI, task) that could invoke it when the allowlist changes. The documented cache-consistency contract is unimplemented — allowlist changes propagate only via the 60-second TTL expiry — and the function ships as dead API surface implying an invalidation flow that does not exist.

[ADVISORY] The identical `if upsampling_enabled: final_columns = transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling(query_columns)` block is repeated at three sites (~230-234, ~275-278, ~294-297) even though `final_columns` is already initialized from `query_columns` at the top of the function. The next query path added to `_get_event_stats` can silently miss the transform and return un-upsampled counts; applying the transform once before the branching would delete two of the three duplicated blocks.

[ADVISORY] No test exercises the cache-hit branch of `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` (each test issues a single request, so only the miss-then-set path runs) nor `invalidate_upsampling_cache` — the caching layer that is the PR's headline 'performance optimization' is unverified. A regression in the cache-key construction or the cached-result AND logic would ship unnoticed and serve wrong upsampling decisions across requests for up to the TTL window.

[ADVISORY] The new `upsampled_count` function is registered without `private=True` (unlike the adjacent function it was appended after), exposing the internal `sum(sample_weight)` aggregation as a user-selectable discover function. Any user can pass yAxis=upsampled_count() on a non-allowlisted org or a transactions query and get a sum over unpopulated sample_weight values — 0 counts or a snuba unknown-column error — with no signal that the function depends on project-level sampling state.

[BUG] The helper returns True for the errors dataset ('if dataset == errors: return True') but 'upsampled_count' is registered only in discover's function_converter (discover.py:1041-1052), so a dataset=errors events-stats request on an allowlisted project sends 'upsampled_count() as count' to the errors resolver, which has no such function. Previously valid dataset=errors&yAxis=count() queries start failing with an invalid-function/InvalidSearchQuery error (400) for any organization once a project is added to the allowlist.

[BUG] _is_error_focused_query uses a raw substring check for 'event.type:error', so negated queries like '!event.type:error' and OR-queries like '(event.type:error OR event.type:transaction)' are classified as error-focused and get count() replaced with sum(sample_weight). On allowlisted projects, a '!event.type:error' chart aggregates only non-error rows whose sample_weight is 0/absent, so the series collapses to ~0 instead of the transaction counts it returned before this change.

[BUG] The diff adds a git submodule gitlink 'sentry-repo' (mode 160000 pointing at a5d290951de) with no corresponding .gitmodules entry anywhere in the diff. CI and fresh contributor checkouts cannot resolve the submodule (empty directory or clone failure), and the pointer is unrelated to the upsampling feature.

[ADVISORY] The transform relies on 'the database schema to ensure sample_weight exists for all events in allowlisted projects' and skips null handling, but the only sample_rate writer in this diff is the test factory (_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling in testutils/factories.py) — no production ingestion path, backfill, or fallback for events without sample_weight ships here. Adding a project to the allowlist before its events carry sample_weight (pre-rollout or never-sampled events) makes sum(sample_weight) evaluate to 0, so count() charts for that project silently read zero.

[ADVISORY] invalidate_upsampling_cache has no caller anywhere in the diff, and its cache key embeds the exact sorted project-id set, so it cannot invalidate the other (org, project-subset) keys an org has accumulated. When the allowlist changes, every cached subset except the exact one passed in stays stale for up to 60s and operators have no code path to force a refresh, despite the docstring promising 'cache consistency across the system'.

[ADVISORY] The 'performance optimization' wraps options.get('issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist') — an in-process lookup against sentry's options manager — in a Redis cache.get/cache.set pair that runs on every events-stats request, including transactions/metrics/spans queries that can never upsample. Every stats request gains one cache roundtrip (two on miss) that the pre-diff path did not have, so the change adds tail latency to all event charts under cache pressure instead of removing any cost.

[ADVISORY] Of the four upsampling application sites added in organization_events_stats.py, the tests cover only the non-topEvents/non-RPC discover path; no test exercises topEvents with the allowlist set, useRpc=true with the allowlist set, dataset=errors, or the cache logic in is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects/invalidate_upsampling_cache (tests/sentry/api/helpers/test_error_upsampling.py tests only the four private helpers). A regression in the topEvents/RPC transform sites or in the cache-hit branch (error_upsampling.py:31-32) would ship silently and misreport counts on dashboards that use those paths.

[ADVISORY] In the topEvents path only timeseries_columns is transformed while selected_columns=self.get_field_list(...) is left raw, so a request carrying field=count() aggregates the grouping/ranking columns with raw count() while the series uses upsampled_count(). Top-events responses mix raw and upsampled counts for the same statistic, so displayed series values and field values/ordering disagree for allowlisted projects.

[ADVISORY] The new upsampled_count SnQLFunction omits private=True (unlike the adjacent internal function in the same converter), leaving it invokable by any user in arbitrary discover queries regardless of the allowlist. A user on a non-allowlisted project can request yAxis=upsampled_count() and get raw sum(sample_weight), which reads 0/garbage wherever weights are not populated — an unsupported aggregation exposed on the public query surface.

[ADVISORY] The same two-line 'if upsampling_enabled: final_columns = transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling(query_columns)' block is repeated at three sites (plus a dead 'final_columns = query_columns' initialization and a should_upsample→upsampling_enabled alias) although the transform is pure and could run once before the branches. Any future extension of the transformation (e.g., handling more aggregates) must be replicated at three sites, and missing one silently leaves that query path untransformed.

[BUG] The diff adds a stray git submodule 'sentry-repo' (gitlink a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a) at the repository root that is completely unrelated to the upsampling feature. Once merged, every checkout/CI run that resolves submodules tries to fetch an unregistered nested repo at that commit, breaking clone/CI for all consumers; this is pure scope drift with no traceability to the stated requirement.

[BUG] _should_apply_sample_weight_transform returns True unconditionally for the errors dataset, but 'upsampled_count' is registered only in the discover dataset's function_converter (src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py:1041-1052), so errors-dataset queries get count() rewritten to a function the errors dataset cannot resolve. Any events-stats query routed to dataset=errors for an allowlisted org fails SnQL function resolution and errors out instead of returning stats; if dataset=errors is not reachable from this endpoint, the errors branch is dead code and the helper's claimed errors-dataset support is illusory — either way the dataset dispatch and the function registration contradict each other.

[BUG] _is_error_focused_query classifies any query containing the substring 'event.type:error' as error-focused, including negations like '!event.type:error' and mixed queries like 'event.type:transaction OR event.type:error'. For allowlisted projects on the discover dataset, a query that excludes or mixes non-error events gets count() rewritten to sum(sample_weight) over rows the diff's own docstring says have no sample_weight for transactions, returning zeroed or undercounted buckets instead of real transaction counts.

[BUG] When upsampling is enabled only the y-axis literal 'count()' is rewritten; equations (get_equation_list), selected_columns/raw_groupby (get_field_list), and other count-based y-axes such as count_if(...) are passed through untransformed. A single response mixes weighted and unweighted numbers — e.g., yAxis count() reports the upsampled 10 while a count_if(...) y-axis or an equation referencing count() reports the raw sampled 1 — so dashboards on allowlisted projects display internally inconsistent figures with no indication to the user.

[BUG] The upsampling transform is applied to the use_rpc query paths (run_top_events_timeseries_query/run_timeseries_query), but 'upsampled_count' exists only in sentry-side discover.py's function_converter while RPC query resolution happens on the snuba side, and no test in the diff exercises use_rpc with the transformed columns. An allowlisted-org stats request that routes through RPC sends 'upsampled_count() as count' to a resolver that does not register that function and fails, and the shipped tests only cover the non-RPC path so this ships unverified.

[ADVISORY] invalidate_upsampling_cache has no caller anywhere in the diff, and its semantics cannot work: the cache key embeds the exact sorted project-id tuple, so deleting one key cannot invalidate the other project-combination keys already cached for the same organization. The 60-second staleness the cache introduces has no mitigation path — allowlist changes take up to 60s to propagate everywhere — and the shipped invalidation helper is dead code that gives operators a false sense of cache consistency.

[ADVISORY] The 'performance optimization' replaces sentry's in-process options lookup (options.get is served from an in-process cache) with a remote cache.get/cache.set round-trip on every events-stats request, and the _are_all_projects_error_upsampled docstring ('reads the allowlist configuration fresh each time... latest configuration state') is contradicted by the caller's 60s cache. Every stats request — the overwhelming majority from organizations not on the allowlist — now pays a remote cache round-trip to avoid a local dict lookup, adding latency on a hot dashboard path while introducing 60s staleness; the optimization is a net regression and the expansion (cache + invalidation machinery) is not justified by any stated requirement.

[ADVISORY] _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling mutates the shared Factories.store_event path for the entire test suite and embeds production data-shaping logic (deriving sample_rate from contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate) in test utilities, with no corresponding production ingest change in this diff, plus two bare 'except Exception: pass' blocks that silently swallow malformed context shapes. Any existing or future test that stores events carrying an error_sampling context now silently produces different snuba rows (sample_weight), and the upsampling feature is validated only against test-factory-shaped data rather than the production ingest path that must populate sample_weight.

[ADVISORY] No test in the diff exercises is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects (the caching entry point, including the cache-hit short-circuit 'return cached_result and _should_apply_sample_weight_transform(...)') or invalidate_upsampling_cache. The headline 'performance optimization' logic — cache keying, TTL, and the cache-hit gate — ships with zero coverage, so a regression there (e.g., caching a dataset-dependent value or a key collision) would reach production silently.

[ADVISORY] The transform is applied inline at three separate branches (top-events at 232-233, RPC at 276-277, standard at 295-296) instead of once immediately after the eligibility check, alongside a redundant alias (upsampling_enabled = should_upsample). A future fourth query path added to _get_event_stats must remember to re-apply the transform or it will silently serve untransformed, undercounted counts for allowlisted projects; computing final_columns once after the eligibility check would delete two of the three branches and the alias.

[ADVISORY] upsampled_count is registered without private=True (unlike its neighboring function in the same list), making it a user-callable aggregate on any discover query, entirely outside the allowlist gating the rest of the diff builds. A user can invoke upsampled_count() directly on non-allowlisted projects where the diff's own comments say sample_weight is not guaranteed to exist, getting zeroed or undercounted results instead of count() — a new public query-language surface not traceable to the stated requirement and unenforced by the eligibility invariant.

[ADVISORY] Drive-by rewording of the topEvents validation error message ('If topEvents needs to be at least 1' to 'topEvents needs to be at least 1') is unrelated to the upsampling feature. An API error string changes silently inside a feature PR; any client or test matching the old text breaks, and the change is untraceable to the upsampling requirement.

[BUG] _should_apply_sample_weight_transform returns True unconditionally for the errors dataset, and the endpoint then rewrites count() into 'upsampled_count() as count', but the upsampled_count SnQL function is registered only in discover.py's function_converter (discover.py:1041-1052) — the errors dataset's registry is untouched by this diff. Any ?dataset=errors events-stats request from an allowlisted org with yAxis=count() — a query that works today — fails SnQL parsing with a 400 once the allowlist option is populated; the diff's own unit test (test_should_apply_sample_weight_transform, asserting errors -> True) codifies the broken branch instead of catching it.

[BUG] upsampled_count is registered as a user-invocable SnQL function (no private=True, unlike its neighbor at line 1039), so the allowlist eligibility gate in the endpoint helper does not cover direct use of the function in user-authored queries. Any user can send yAxis=upsampled_count() on the discover dataset for non-allowlisted projects and get sum(sample_weight) presented as an official count — deflated where weights are NULL/absent, inflated where events were sampled — silently disagreeing with count() on the same chart, with the allowlist guard completely bypassed.

[BUG] _is_error_focused_query decides error-focus by substring-matching the raw query string, so '!event.type:error' (negation) and 'event.type:transaction OR event.type:error' (mixed) both match, while event.type:'error' (quoted value) does not. Negated or mixed-type discover queries on allowlisted projects get sum(sample_weight) applied to non-error events — which the helper's own docstring (lines 106-107) says lack the column — producing a query error or counts that drop those events to 0, while quoted-value error queries silently skip upsampling, so identical dashboards show inconsistent numbers depending on quote style.

[BUG] The transform and the upsampled_count aggregate assume sample_weight is populated and non-NULL for every event in allowlisted projects, but the diff contains no migration, column default, backfill, or production ingestion path that writes it — the only sample_rate writer added anywhere is the test-factory helper _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling (factories.py:344-359). In production, events with NULL or 0 sample_weight contribute 0 to sum(sample_weight), so allowlisted-org counts are silently wrong while the new endpoint tests pass only because the factory injects contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate — a green suite that never exercises the production data path the feature depends on.

[BUG] Only the y-axis columns are transformed, and transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling (error_upsampling.py:92-95) rewrites only an exact alias-free 'count()' literal — count_unique/count_if/count_web_transactions, aliased forms like 'count() as total', and any count() in the top-events selected_columns/equations passed at organization_events_stats.py:255-256 remain raw counts. A single top-events response can mix upsampled timeseries counts with raw table counts for the same time window, and the stringly-typed rewrite hard-couples the endpoint to SnQL aliasing conventions that break silently if either side changes.

[ADVISORY] is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects runs an unconditional remote cache.get (plus cache.set on miss, error_upsampling.py:30/38) on every _get_event_stats call to memoize options.get, which Sentry already serves from an in-process option cache. Every organization-events-stats request — the hot dashboard-polling path — now pays a network roundtrip to the cache backend (and a write on miss, with stampede potential) where the diff previously made no remote call; the 'performance optimization' is a net pessimization adding latency and cache load to the hottest stats endpoint.

[ADVISORY] invalidate_upsampling_cache has no caller anywhere in the diff, and its per-(organization, project-tuple) key deletion cannot implement its documented contract: a global allowlist change affects every org/project-subset key, and no hook exists on option changes. A future maintainer wiring allowlist edits to this function will believe cache consistency is enforced while every other key stays stale; today the exported function is dead code and the only staleness bound is the undocumented 60s TTL.

[ADVISORY] The cache key embeds hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids))) (same at line 73) instead of the ids themselves, and hash is not injective, so two distinct project-id sets that collide share one cache entry. A request for project set B can be served the allowlist verdict cached for project set A, flipping upsampling on/off for the wrong project set and returning wrong counts; embedding the sorted ids directly in the key removes the failure mode at zero cost.

[ADVISORY] Allowlist membership is tested with 'project_id in allowlist' against the raw option list — a linear scan per project — instead of converting the allowlist to a set once before the loop. Cost is O(projects-per-query x allowlist-size) on every cache miss of a hot endpoint, scaling linearly with the very allowlist this feature grows project by project, for a one-line set() fix.

[ADVISORY] The same two-line 'if upsampling_enabled: final_columns = transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling(query_columns)' block is duplicated at three branch sites (232-233, 274-275, 295-296), plus a redundant 'upsampling_enabled = should_upsample' alias at line 226. A fourth execution path added later must remember to re-apply the transform or it silently serves untransformed columns; transforming once before the branches deletes two branches and the alias, leaving one place to update.

[ADVISORY] The diff adds a git submodule gitlink ('sentry-repo', mode 160000, commit a5d290951de) at the repository root that is unrelated to the upsampling feature and unexplained by it. Merging registers a phantom submodule that every CI checkout and contributor clone must resolve (or fails against), and the pointer silently pins/drifts against the referenced commit; this has the shape of an accidental 'git add' of a nested checkout and should be dropped from the PR.

[ADVISORY] The brand-new module sentry.api.helpers.error_upsampling is added to the per-module override list that relaxes strict checks (alongside legacy modules being grandfathered), so new production code is born exempt from the strictness the list exists to phase out. Type errors in the new eligibility/transform logic — exactly the stringly-typed query-rewriting code most likely to break — are invisible to CI from day one; new modules should be held to the strict standard rather than added to the legacy exemption list.

[ADVISORY] No test in the diff exercises the transformed query end-to-end for dataset=errors, the top-events path, the use_rpc path, or the cache/invalidate functions — the endpoint tests cover only the default discover, non-RPC, non-top-events path with the options module fully mocked. The errors-dataset registry gap (which a single dataset=errors endpoint test would have caught), a transform regression in top-events/RPC column handling, or a cache-staleness bug all ship green; because every test replaces the options module, the option key string itself is never validated against the real options registry either.

[BUG] The PR commits a git submodule gitlink `sentry-repo` (mode 160000 pointing at commit a5d290951de) with no corresponding `.gitmodules` entry anywhere in the diff — an accidental commit of a nested checkout, unrelated to the upsampling feature. Any submodule-aware clone or CI step running `git submodule update --init` fails with 'No submodule mapping found in .gitmodules for path sentry-repo', and every developer's working tree carries a dangling pointer that shows as a perpetually dirty submodule.

[BUG] `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` returns True unconditionally for the `errors` dataset, but the `upsampled_count` function it rewrites `count()` into is registered only in discover's `function_converter` (discover.py:1041-1052), not in the errors dataset's converter. For an allowlisted org querying the errors dataset with count() — a path the helper's own unit test asserts is taken (`assert _should_apply_sample_weight_transform(errors, self.request) is True`) — query construction fails on the unknown function instead of returning stats; if dataset=errors is unreachable on this endpoint, the branch is dead code contradicting its own test, either way the implementation no longer matches the stated intent of supporting errors-dataset upsampling.

[ADVISORY] The only code in this diff that writes sampling data is a test-factory helper setting `sample_rate`, while the query path aggregates `Column("sample_weight")` (discover.py:1048) — no production writer for `sample_weight`, and no registration or management path for the `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` option, exists anywhere in the PR. The shipped read path depends on an out-of-diff ingestion change; if that half was dropped during iteration, allowlisted projects' `count()` silently becomes `sum(sample_weight)` over a column nothing populates in production, collapsing counts to zero or erroring — the tests only pass because the factory hack simulates the missing pipeline.

[ADVISORY] The new `upsampled_count` SnQLFunction omits `private=True` (unlike its neighbor in the same converter), exposing an internal aggregation that sums `sample_weight` with no allowlist gate inside the function itself to arbitrary user queries on the discover dataset. Any user on any project — allowlisted or not — can query `upsampled_count()` and get `sum(sample_weight)` values this PR never validates for non-sampled projects, silently expanding the public query surface beyond the accepted intent of an internal-only transform.

[BUG] `_is_error_focused_query` uses a raw substring check (`"event.type:error" in query`), so queries that merely contain the token — including negations like `!event.type:error` or the string inside quoted free-text — are classified as error-focused. An allowlisted org running `!event.type:error` on the discover dataset gets the `sum(sample_weight)` transform applied to a query that matches non-error events (where this diff's own docstring states sample_weight doesn't exist), producing query errors or zero counts instead of the untransformed result the user asked for.

[ADVISORY] `invalidate_upsampling_cache` has no caller anywhere in the diff, and `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled`'s docstring (lines 50-53) claims fresh-read semantics ('reads the allowlist configuration fresh each time... This is intentional') that the caller's 60-second cache.set (line 38) directly defeats. After an operator changes `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist`, stats endpoints keep applying or skipping the upsampled transform for up to 60 seconds with no way to force a refresh, and the documented consistency mechanism is untestable dead code — two contradictory consistency models from different review iterations shipped together without reconciliation.

[ADVISORY] Every organization-events-stats request now unconditionally performs a cache.get (and on miss a cache.set keyed by org id plus hash of the project-id set) before any dataset or allowlist check, so the 'performance optimization' adds a remote cache roundtrip to 100% of traffic including orgs and datasets that can never be upsampled. The common case — non-allowlisted orgs and transactions/metrics queries — gets strictly slower via a Redis/memcached roundtrip per stats request plus near-constant misses and writes from the unbounded per-org-per-project-set key space, inverting the stated objective of the optimization.

[ADVISORY] The transformation is wired into three execution paths (top-events, use_rpc, standard timeseries) but every new test exercises only the standard non-RPC timeseries path, leaving the top-events and RPC rewrites completely untested. A regression in the top-events path — the primary dashboard/issues-widget route, where the transformed `upsampled_count() as count` select must still interoperate with `orderby=-count()` and the raw groupbys — would ship silently and corrupt top-events counts for allowlisted orgs.

[ADVISORY] `upsampling_enabled = should_upsample` is a contentless alias and `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling(query_columns)` is duplicated verbatim in three mutually exclusive branches (lines ~232, ~274, ~292) when a single conditional assignment before the branches would serve all three. Every future change to the transformation wiring must be replicated in three places with three copies of self-justifying comments ('This late transformation ensures we use the most current schema assumptions'), and an editor of one branch can silently miss the other two.

[ADVISORY] `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` is wired into the shared `Factories.store_event` path used by the entire test suite, and it swallows all failures with two bare `except Exception: pass` blocks (lines 351-352, 356-357). Any existing or future test storing `contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate` silently gains a `sample_rate` field it never asked for, and malformed contexts are silently dropped with no signal, masking exactly the ingestion behavior this helper was added to simulate.

[ADVISORY] The PR silently rewrites a user-facing API error string from 'If topEvents needs to be at least 1' to 'topEvents needs to be at least 1', a drive-by change unrelated to the upsampling objective. Clients, dashboards, or out-of-tree tests matching the old message text break without this contract change ever being part of the accepted scope.

[ADVISORY] The brand-new 140-line module and its test are added to the mypy suppression lists at birth (lines 176 and ~464) instead of being made type-clean, so type errors in `error_upsampling.py` are invisible to CI from day one. Future refactors of the helper can introduce type breakage that no CI gate catches, and the suppression entry indicates the module was pushed through review without resolving its type errors — a quality bar lowered without explicit acceptance.

[BUG] _is_error_focused_query gates the upsampling transform on a raw substring match for 'event.type:error' in the lowercased query string, so any discover query that contains that substring while also matching non-error events passes the error-only gate. For an allowlisted org, a user query like 'event.type:error OR event.type:transaction' or the negation '!event.type:error' gets count() rewritten to sum(sample_weight) over a result set containing transaction events, which this diff's own docstring states have no sample_weight — the stats endpoint then returns counts that silently exclude those events (sum skips rows without weights) or fails query validation resolving the column on the transactions side of the discover union, corrupting dashboard totals for exactly the queries users plausibly run.

[BUG] _should_apply_sample_weight_transform returns True unconditionally for the errors dataset, but the 'upsampled_count' function it emits is only registered in discover.py's function_converter, so 'upsampled_count() as count' cannot be resolved on the errors dataset. An events-stats request with dataset=errors against an allowlisted project — a query that worked before this change — now emits an unregistered SnQL function and fails query validation, returning an error to the user instead of stats; the helper explicitly enables the errors dataset path while the function definition was only added to one dataset.

[ADVISORY] The new 'upsampled_count' SnQLFunction is registered without private=True (unlike the neighboring internal function directly above it), making it directly invocable from user-supplied query strings and bypassing the allowlist eligibility gate that governs the automatic count() transformation. Any authenticated user can request upsampled_count() on projects that are not on the allowlist, where sample_weight is unpopulated per this diff's own assumptions, and receive zero/garbage counts or query errors; the allowlist control the rest of the feature enforces is circumvented simply by naming the function, and an internal aggregation detail is leaked into the public query grammar.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The eligibility check performs a remote cache GET (and a cache SET on miss) before the pure in-process dataset/request checks, so every events-stats request pays the round-trip even for queries that can never be upsampled. Adds Redis latency and per-org-x-project-subset cache-write amplification to one of the hottest chart endpoints for transactions/metrics/spans queries whose cached answer is never used; ordering the dataset check first would avoid the remote call entirely on those paths.

adjudication.rationale: In `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` (new `src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py`), the function does `cache.get(cache_key)` (and `cache.set(...)` on miss) before checking `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform(dataset, request)`. Since `_get_event_stats` now calls `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(snuba_params, organization, dataset, request)` unconditionally in `organization_events_stats.py`, even requests for datasets that can never be upsampled (e.g., `transactions` or non-error discover queries) will still pay the cache round-trip; only after that will `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` return False. The finding’s suggested reordering (dataset/request checks first, cache only on eligible paths) is directly supported by the diff and is a concrete performance concern on a hot endpoint, not a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Only the exact string 'count()' is rewritten; count_if(...), aliased variants like 'count() as total', and whitespace variants such as 'count( )' pass through unweighted.
